rationale: A defensible broadening of the archive's best-performing bet leg (adding purchased intangibles so acquisition-built firms are not mis-scored as zero), but it changes two things at once — the intangible measure *and* the switch from ZSCORE to IND_ZSCORE — so a change in alpha will not be attributable to either, and the added `intan` stock is a book-value item that the "missing from book value" mechanism explicitly does not apply to.

A genuine single-lever ablation (1-year vs 3-year accrual gate) on the archive's strongest mechanism, with an interpretable outcome either way — persistence of earnings quality versus transient accrual reversal — and no sign or coverage inconsistency.

Sign and construction are internally consistent and the industry-relative gate with zero-fill genuinely repairs the 4.7% coverage of the gen-0 winner, but because IND_RANK is a strictly positive [0,1] weight applied to raw accruals across essentially the full universe, the signal risks loading heavily on plain Sloan accruals — the proposal should be judged against a vanilla-accrual benchmark, not against zero.

Substituting a firm-relative (time-series rank) accrual frame for the cross-sectional level is the one dimension the archive has never varied and separates business-model accrual intensity from transitory accounting discretion; the main caveat is that TS_RANK over five annual observations is a very coarse statistic and may be dominated by ties and noise.

A legitimate out-of-channel replication that would discriminate between "expensed intangible capital" and "R&D/tech-specific" explanations, but `COALESCE(xad, 0)` converts a reporting decision into an economic zero for the majority of firms, so the bet leg will behave largely as an advertiser/non-advertiser indicator and any result will be confounded with the known advertising-expenditure anomaly.

Since RANK(NEG(x)) ≈ 1 − RANK(x) and the accrual leg is identical to the archived signal's, this expression is algebraically ≈ AcquiredIntangibleAccrualInflation minus the plain working-capital accrual z-score — so it is a linear combination of an already-evaluated signal and vanilla Sloan accruals rather than a new corner of the joint distribution, and the "impairment" leg is in practice dominated by routine amortization.
